findings.subtopic: School-device restrictions, educational-technology registration, and student-data use
findings.regulation: Proposed Fostering Optimal Classroom Use of Screens (FOCUS) Act, S10685
findings.ai_system_type: Generative AI, conversational AI, AI companions, and AI trained on student data
findings.effective_date: If enacted, the first 1 August after becoming law
findings.what_changed: New York Senate Bill S10685 was introduced and referred to the Senate Rules Committee. The proposal would limit school-issued devices, prohibit generative AI, conversational AI, and AI companions on those devices, require educational-technology providers to register with the Attorney General, and restrict use of student personally identifiable information, including excluding AI training from permitted internal business operations.
findings.previous_position: The stored 2026-08-22 New York legislative baseline did not identify this newly introduced proposal.
findings.new_position: A pending New York bill now proposes specific AI and data-processing restrictions for schools, school devices, and educational-technology providers. It is not enacted law.
findings.legal_significance: If enacted, the bill would create statutory restrictions on AI-enabled school technology, provider registration and certification duties, enforcement exposure, and student-data processing limits.
findings.business_significance: Educational-technology and device providers serving New York schools may need product exclusions, registration evidence, independent performance support, change re-registration, contract revisions, and limits preventing student data from being used for AI training.
findings.technical_significance: Products may need controls that block prohibited AI services on school-issued devices, prevent unrelated media access, segregate student data from model-training pipelines, and record significant product modifications.
